title: Derived adic completeness
statement:
Let $E/\Ql$ be finite, with uniformizer $\pi_E$, and let
$\mathcal O_{E,X}=p_X^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ and $(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_X$ be
the integral and finite coefficient sheaves of
[sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. A complex
$K\in D(X_{\Proet},\mathcal O_E)$ is *derived complete* if its canonical map

$$
K\longrightarrow R\varprojlim_n\bigl(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,X}}(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_X\bigr)
$$

is an isomorphism. For
$K_n=K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,X}}(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_X$, the canonical
transitions satisfy the derived reduction identities
$K_{n+1}\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^{n+1})_X}(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_X\simeq K_n$;
a compatible tower with these identities is called *normalized*.

Normalization is a property of the complexes $K_n$; their cohomology sheaves
$H^q(K_n)$ need not form a normalized tower under the ordinary tensor product.

proof.text: Unpack the notation with $X$ an arbitrary scheme, $\ell$ prime and $n\geq1$. Put $R=\mathcal O_{E,X}$ and $B_n=(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_X$. The valuation ring, uniformizer, quotient rings and quotient homomorphisms are the data of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Apply the continuous-ring construction of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and then the functor on ring objects of [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] to obtain compatible maps $R\to B_{n+1}\to B_n$. The ambient category is the unbounded Layer B category $D(\Mod_R)$ of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], applied to the commutative condensed coefficient ring $\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ and its pulled-back ring object $R$. This invokes the ambient-category row, not the constructible subcategory or the general left-derived existence clause of that node; its relative derived tensor is that of [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. No identification of $R$ with a completed constant coefficient sheaf is made. To apply ringed-site lemmas to these module objects, specialize [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure] to $\mathcal A=\Ab$ and the essentially small site $C=X_{\mathrm{proét}}$: its tensor is $a(\mathcal F\otimes_p\mathcal G)$, its unit is the constant $\mathbf Z$-sheaf, and $a$ is strong symmetric monoidal. Here $a$ is abelian sheafification, not an objectwise tensor assumed already to be a sheaf. The Layer B clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom] derives the relative tensor of module objects over $R$; thus it is the balanced tensor over this ring object that must be compared with sectionwise module tensor. With the usual small-site/coefficient-universe convention, [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] identifies internal $R$-modules with sectionwise modules over the reconstructed ring sheaf, preserving underlying abelian sheaves and maps identically. An internal balanced bilinear map is precisely a sectionwise balanced bilinear map compatible with restrictions: the two action equations are the same equations on sections. Consequently their representing relative tensor products agree under this equivalence. Since it preserves underlying sheaves and maps, it also preserves exact complexes and the tensor tests for flatness and K-flatness. Thus the K-flat and product arguments below take place over this same ring sheaf $R$.

source.place: statement, coefficient sheaves and ambient derived category

proof.text: By [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], choose a K-flat representative $P$ of $K$ whose terms are flat $R$-modules. Derived extension of scalars [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars] is computed by this representative, so $P_n=P\otimes_R B_n$ represents $K_n$ as a complex of $B_n$-modules. Restriction of scalars leaves the underlying objects and maps unchanged by clause 1 of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. Its exactness can be checked directly in the sectionwise-module presentation of step 1: a kernel is the underlying kernel with the restricted action, and a cokernel is the underlying quotient with the induced action. Restricting the ring action therefore preserves both and leaves the exact underlying sequence unchanged. This is the exact restriction used in [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars]; no exactness of extension of scalars is asserted. Thus we can regard all $P_n$ as $R$-complexes. The maps $P_{n+1}\to P_n$ send $p\otimes b$ to $p\otimes\bar b$, and the unit maps $c_n:P\to P_n$ send $p$ to $p\otimes1$. They are chain maps and satisfy $t_nc_{n+1}=c_n$ strictly, since both send $p$ to $p\otimes1$. This constructs the reduction cone appearing in the definition.

source.place: Tag 06YS, lemma-K-flat-resolution; Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change, for identity-topos coefficient change

proof.text: Countable products of $R$-module sheaves are exact by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact], which applies to an arbitrary sheaf of commutative rings and hence to the pulled-back ring $R$. By clause 2 of [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence], the product $Q=\prod_n K_n$ in $D(\Mod_R)$ exists and is represented by $\prod_nP_n$. Let $s:Q\to Q$ have $n$-th component $t_n\operatorname{pr}_{n+1}$. By [def-weil-derived-limit], $R\varprojlim K_n$ means the homotopy limit specified by a distinguished triangle $L\to Q\xrightarrow{1-s}Q\to L[1]$, and it exists by clause 1 of [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence]. On the strict representatives it is modeled by $\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$. The compatible unit maps give $c=(c_n):P\to\prod_nP_n$ and $(1-s)c=0$; the comparison to this cone is the chain map $(c,0)$: explicitly write $L^i=Q^i\oplus Q^{i-1}$ with $d_L(x,y)=(d_Qx,(1-s)x-d_Qy)$, so $d_L(c(p),0)=(c(d_Pp),0)$. The displayed completeness condition requires this specified reduction comparison to be an isomorphism in the derived category, equivalently a quasi-isomorphism of these representatives. This retains the coherent reduction maps and their strict zero homotopy; it does not replace the comparison by an unrelated isomorphism between the underlying objects. The condition does not depend on the chosen representative. Let $P'$ be another K-flat representative of $K$ with flat terms. The isomorphism $P\cong P'$ in $D(\Mod_R)$ is represented by a roof $P\leftarrow W\to P'$ of chain maps that are quasi-isomorphisms; composing with a resolution of $W$ from [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], we may take $W$ K-flat with flat terms. Write $a\colon W\to P$ and $a'\colon W\to P'$ for the legs. Since [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars] computes $B_n\otimes^{\mathbf L}_R-$ by applying $B_n\otimes_R-$ to K-flat complexes, $a\otimes_RB_n\colon W\otimes_RB_n\to P_n$ represents the isomorphism obtained by applying that derived functor to $a$, so it is a quasi-isomorphism; likewise for $a'$. These maps commute strictly with the transitions and the units, since $w\otimes b\mapsto a(w)\otimes b$ and $w\mapsto a(w)\otimes1$. By clause 2 of [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence], cohomology commutes with these products, so $\prod_n(a\otimes_RB_n)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The induced map of the complexes $L$ respects the degreewise split exact sequences $0\to Q[-1]\to L\to Q\to0$, given by $y\mapsto(0,y)$ and $(x,y)\mapsto x$. By the five lemma on their long exact cohomology sequences, it is a quasi-isomorphism. It commutes strictly with the comparisons $(c,0)$. By two-out-of-three for quasi-isomorphisms, the comparison for $P$ is a quasi-isomorphism exactly when the one for $W$ is, and exactly when the one for $P'$ is.

source.place: Tag 08TC, definition-derived-limit and paragraph following it; Bhatt-Scholze, Definition 3.5.2 gives the completeness convention (only the convention, not a coefficient comparison)

proof.text: For the normalization assertion, apply [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings] to the sheaf-ring homomorphism $R\to B_{n+1}$ and the representative $P$ of step 2. Its hypotheses hold because $P$ is K-flat with flat terms. Thus $P\otimes_R B_{n+1}$ is K-flat over $B_{n+1}$. Consequently [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars] computes $K_{n+1}\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{B_{n+1}}B_n$ by $(P\otimes_R B_{n+1})\otimes_{B_{n+1}}B_n$. Here the second tensor is over $B_{n+1}$, not over $R$; no flatness of $B_n$ over $B_{n+1}$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0G7E, lemma-pullback-K-flat, identity-topos coefficient change; Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change

proof.text: The last complex is isomorphic to $P\otimes_R B_n$ by the maps $(p\otimes a)\otimes b\mapsto p\otimes\bar a b$ and $p\otimes b\mapsto(p\otimes1)\otimes b$. These formulas are balanced over $R$ and $B_{n+1}$ and inverse: $\bar a b$ can be moved to the second tensor factor by the balancing relation. They commute with the differential, which acts only on $p$. The coequalizer definition of relative tensor and extension of scalars [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] makes the formulas maps of sheaves, and step 2 identifies the right-hand complex with $K_n$. This proves the derived reduction identity. For a longer chain $B_r\to B_m\to B_n$ both possible composites send $((p\otimes a)\otimes b)\otimes c$ to $p\otimes\bar a\bar b c$; the unit maps send $p\otimes a$ to $(p\otimes a)\otimes1$, which becomes $p\otimes\bar a$. Hence the identities are coherent and induce exactly the given transition maps. A normalized tower requires these derived reduction isomorphisms for its transition-induced comparisons, not unrelated isomorphisms between levels.

source.place: Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition, proof specialized to coefficient changes; the displayed balanced tensor calculation supplies the elementary step

proof.text: The cohomology warning is substantive. Set $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ and take any nonempty $X$. The finite discrete rings $\mathbf Z/\ell^n$ give constant finite ring sheaves $B_n$: for a finite discrete set its condensed sheaf is the corresponding finite coproduct of the terminal sheaf, and geometric inverse image preserves this coproduct. By [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback] and [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact], $p_X^*$ is exact, so the finite-ring kernel computations can equally be pulled back. Take $K=[R\xrightarrow{\ell}R]$ in degrees $-1,0$. It is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site], as its two terms are free of rank one. Its reductions are therefore $[B_n\xrightarrow{\ell}B_n]$, a normalized tower by steps 4-5. Their $H^{-1}$ is the constant sheaf associated to $\ell^{n-1}\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$, nonzero and isomorphic to $\mathbf F_\ell$. The transition sends the generator $\ell^n\bmod\ell^{n+1}$ to zero modulo $\ell^n$. Consequently $H^{-1}(K_{n+1})\otimes_{B_{n+1}}B_n\to H^{-1}(K_n)$ is zero between nonzero copies of the constant residue-field sheaf, and is not an isomorphism. Thus derived normalization does not assert ordinary-tensor normalization on cohomology. The only finite-ring arithmetic used is that $\ell a=0\bmod\ell^n$ exactly when $a$ is divisible by $\ell^{n-1}$.

source.place: last paragraph, cohomology need not be an ordinary normalized tower; explicit two-term example supplied by the worker
